messages.subject: FA calculation internally in bilat.symmetry
parts:
Hello Geomorph users,

I am looking into the source code for bilat.symmetry in geomorph v3.2.1 to understand how FA is calculated internally in bilat.symmetry. 

The source code for bilat.symmetry contains the following code snippet:

mn.DA <- DA.mns[, , 1] - DA.mns[, , 2]
...
FA.component <- simplify2array(lapply(1:n.ind, function(j) {
    t(matrix(FA.component[j, ], k, p)) + mn.shape - mn.DA
}))

It can be seen that mn.DA refers to difference between 1st and 2nd configuration in DA.mns. DA.mns is the DA.component in bilat.symmetry output where the first 2 configurations are original and relabeled reflections of the 1st specimen. That means FA is calculated for all specimens by the difference between relabed reflection of each specimen and its original configuration plus mean shape of original and relabled reflections of all specimens minus difference between original and relabeled reflections of the 1st specimen.

Based on example data and source code, I replicated bilat.symmetry results:

library(geomorph)
data(scallops)
gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = scallops$coorddata, ind=scallops$ind)

A <- gpagen(scallops$coorddata)
size <- A$Csize
A <- A$coords
n <- dim(A)[3]
k <- dim(A)[2]
p <- dim(A)[1]
ind <- scallops$ind
nind <- nlevels(ind)
land.pairs <- scallops$land.pairs
npairs <- nrow(land.pairs)
A2 <- A
A2[land.pairs[, 1], , ] <- A[land.pairs[, 2], , ]
A2[land.pairs[, 2], , ] <- A[land.pairs[, 1], , ]
A2[, 1, ] <- A2[, 1, ] * (-1)
A_long <- array(c(A, A2), c(p, k, 2 * n))
ind <- factor(rep(ind, 2))
side <- gl(2, n)
gpa.res <- gpagen(A_long)
A_long <- gpa.res$coords

# Table specifying ordering of specimens
# row A_long scallop.sym$DA.component
# 1 ind1 ind1
# 2 ind2 ind1RelabledReflection
# 3 ind3 ind2
# 4 ind4 ind2RelabledReflection
# 5 ind5 ind3
# 6 ind1RelabledReflection ind3RelabledReflection
# 7 ind2RelabledReflection ind4
# 8 ind3RelabledReflection ind4RelabledReflection
# 9 ind4RelabledReflection ind5
# 10         ind5RelabledReflection ind6RelabledReflection

scallop.sym <- bilat.symmetry(A = shape, ind = ind, object.sym = TRUE,
land.pairs=scallops$land.pairs, data = gdf, RRPP = TRUE, iter = 499)

# FA for the 1st specimen (scallop.sym$DA.component is equivalent to the DA.mns used in source code)
fa_a1 <- A_long[,,6] - A_long[,,1] + mshape(A_long) - 
(scallop.sym$DA.component[,,1] - scallop.sym$DA.component[,,2])

# FA for the 4th specimen
fa_a4 <- A_long[,,9] - A_long[,,4] + mshape(A_long) - 
(scallop.sym$DA.component[,,1] - scallop.sym$DA.component[,,2]) # Not (scallop.sym$DA.component[,,8] - scallop.sym$DA.component[,,7])

fa_a1 and fa_a4 are identical to scallop.sym$FA.component[,,1] and scallop.sym$FA.component[,,4], respectively. So I can confirm that bilat.symmetry uses difference between the 1st specimen and its relabled reflection in calculation of FA for all specimens. I do not understand why the difference between original and relabled reflection of the first specimen is subtracted when calculating FA for each specimen. I can understand adding mn.shape to t(matrix(FA.component[j, ], k, p)) allows for more meaningful interpretation and visualization. But why mn.DA is subtracted where mn.DA concerns itself with only the first specimen? The first specimen is so arbitrary.

Thanks.

YF Wen

Dear Prof. Dean, thank you for posting updated code. There is still one thing that I do not particularly understand in the updated code. Calculation of total asymmetry and FA involved relabled reflection minus original specimen:

asymm.component <- avg.side.symm[indsq,] - avg.side.symm[-indsq,]
FA.component <- ind.mns[indsq,] - ind.mns[-indsq,]

Since indsq <- seq(n.side, (n.ind*n.side), n.side), I could tell [indsq,] extracts 2nd, 4th, 6th, ... specimen, which are relabled reflections of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, ... specimen. So total asymmetry and FA involved relabled reflection minus original specimen. In contrast, DA is estimated as follows in updated source code:

mn.DA <- matrix(apply((DA.est[-indsq,] - DA.est[indsq,]),2,mean),byrow=T,nrow=p,ncol=k)

This means DA is obtained by original specimen minus relabeled reflections, the reverse of the direction in which total asymmetry and FA is obtained.

The above code can be translated into the following table:

Original  RelabledReflection      TotalAsymmetry  DA  FA        ReasonableFA
3.2 2      2 - 3.2 = -1.2 ((3.2-2)  + (5.1- 4) + (9.8 - 9) + (12.9-12))/4 = 1 -1.2 - 1 = -2.2 0.2
5.1 4      4 - 5.1 = -1.1 ((3.2-2)  + (5.1- 4) + (9.8 - 9) + (12.9-12))/4 = 1 -1.1 - 1 = -2.1 0.1
9.8 9      9 - 9.8 = -0.8 ((3.2-2)  + (5.1- 4) + (9.8 - 9) + (12.9-12))/4 = 1 -0.8 - 1 = -1.8 -0.2
12.9        12      12 - 12.9 = -0.9         ((3.2-2)  + (5.1- 4) + (9.8 - 9) + (12.9-12))/4 = 1 -0.9 - 1 = -1.9 -0.1

It seems that FA column above is not what is meant by definition of FA. In contrasts, the ReasonableFA column is what we want, which seems cannot be obtained following the ways in which total asymmetry, DA, and FA were calculated in the code. I am not sure if I have missed any part of the code.

Thank you again for your help.

YF Wen

I am looking into the source code for bilat.symmetry in geomorph v3.2.1 to understand how FA is calculated internally in bilat.symmetry. 

 

The source code for bilat.symmetry contains the following code snippet:

 

mn.DA <- DA.mns[, , 1] - DA.mns[, , 2]

...

FA.component <- simplify2array(lapply(1:n.ind, function(j) {

    t(matrix(FA.component[j, ], k, p)) + mn.shape - mn.DA

}))

 

It can be seen that mn.DA refers to difference between 1st and 2nd configuration in DA.mns. DA.mns is the DA.component in bilat.symmetry output where the first 2 configurations are original and relabeled reflections of the 1st specimen. That means FA is calculated for all specimens by the difference between relabed reflection of each specimen and its original configuration plus mean shape of original and relabled reflections of all specimens minus difference between original and relabeled reflections of the 1st specimen.

 

Based on example data and source code, I replicated bilat.symmetry results:

 

library(geomorph)

data(scallops)

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = scallops$coorddata, ind=scallops$ind)

 

A <- gpagen(scallops$coorddata)

size <- A$Csize

A <- A$coords

n <- dim(A)[3]

k <- dim(A)[2]

p <- dim(A)[1]

ind <- scallops$ind

nind <- nlevels(ind)

land.pairs <- scallops$land.pairs

npairs <- nrow(land.pairs)

A2 <- A

A2[land.pairs[, 1], , ] <- A[land.pairs[, 2], , ]

A2[land.pairs[, 2], , ] <- A[land.pairs[, 1], , ]

A2[, 1, ] <- A2[, 1, ] * (-1)

A_long <- array(c(A, A2), c(p, k, 2 * n))

ind <- factor(rep(ind, 2))

side <- gl(2, n)

gpa.res <- gpagen(A_long)

A_long <- gpa.res$coords

 

# Table specifying ordering of specimens

# row   A_long                                                scallop.sym$DA.component

# 1                   ind1                                                     ind1

# 2                   ind2                                                     ind1RelabledReflection

# 3                   ind3                                                     ind2

# 4                   ind4                                                     ind2RelabledReflection

# 5                   ind5                                                     ind3

# 6                   ind1RelabledReflection            ind3RelabledReflection

# 7                   ind2RelabledReflection          ind4

# 8                   ind3RelabledReflection            ind4RelabledReflection

# 9                   ind4RelabledReflection          ind5

# 10             ind5RelabledReflection            ind6RelabledReflection

 

scallop.sym <- bilat.symmetry(A = shape, ind = ind, object.sym = TRUE,

land.pairs=scallops$land.pairs, data = gdf, RRPP = TRUE, iter = 499)

fa_a1 <- A_long[,,6] - A_long[,,1] + mshape(A_long) - 

                        (scallop.sym$DA.component[,,1] - scallop.sym$DA.component[,,2])

                        (scallop.sym$DA.component[,,1] - scallop.sym$DA.component[,,2]) # Not (scallop.sym$DA.component[,,8] - scallop.sym$DA.component[,,7])

I do not understand why the difference between original and relabled reflection of the first specimen is subtracted when calculating FA for each specimen. I can understand adding mn.shape to t(matrix(FA.component[j, ], k, p)) allows for more meaningful interpretation and visualization. Thanks.

 

YF Wen

I read Mardia and Bookstein's paper "Statistical assessment of bilateral symmetry of shapes" and made some progress in understanding method to calculate FA. However, I get different results based on formula provided in this paper.

Equation 3.2 in Mardia's paper is most relevant to how individual magnitude of FA is calculated:

In this formula, X^P and Y^P are Procrustes shape coordinates for original and relabled reflection of all specimens, respectively. X_bar and Y_bar are the mean shape of all X^P and Y^P, respectively. D^2 is squared Procrustes distance between two configurations, which is calculated in squared Euclidean distance. It can be calculated using the dist function, which is how geomorph calculates Procrustes distance.


Using the scallop data from geomorph, I tried to calculate magnitude of FA for the 1st specimen in the dataset following Mardia's equation. You may directly copy and paste the code to replicate my results.


library(geomorph)

library(Morpho)

data(scallops)


gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = scallops$coorddata, ind=scallops$ind)
# Code adapted from bilat.symmetry source code

A <- gpagen(scallops$coorddata)

size <- A$Csize

A <- A$coords

n <- dim(A)[3]

k <- dim(A)[2]

p <- dim(A)[1]

ind <- scallops$ind

nind <- nlevels(ind)

land.pairs <- scallops$land.pairs

npairs <- nrow(land.pairs)

A2 <- A

A2[land.pairs[, 1], , ] <- A[land.pairs[, 2], , ]

A2[land.pairs[, 2], , ] <- A[land.pairs[, 1], , ]

A2[, 1, ] <- A2[, 1, ] * (-1)

A_long <- array(c(A, A2), c(p, k, 2 * n))

ind <- factor(rep(ind, 2))

side <- gl(2, n)

gpa.res <- gpagen(A_long)

# A_long below contains Procrustes shape coordinates for all original specimens and 

# their relabled reflections. Ordering of specimens can be understood through the

# table in the first post of this thread (15 Apr)

A_long <- gpa.res$coords


############################ Total asymmetry for the 1st specimen####################################

TotAsym_score_s1 <- dist(two.d.array(A_long[,,c(1, 6)]))


############################ Magnitude of DA for the 1st specimen#########################################

mean_Original <- mshape(A_long[,,c(1:5)])


mean_RelabRefl <- mshape(A_long[,,c(6:10)])


OriginalRelabRefl <- bindArr(mean_Original, mean_RelabRefl, along = 3)


DA_score <- dist(two.d.array(OriginalRelabRefl))


#######################  FA score calculation using 2 methods ##############################

# Method 1 for calculating FA score: total asymmetry minus DA

FA_score1a_s1 <- sqrt(TotAsym_score_s1^2 - DA_score^2)

FA_score1b_s1 <- TotAsym_score_s1 - DA_score


# Method 2 for calculating FA score: by Madria's algorithm for FA

diff_Orginal_meanOriginal_s1 <- A_long[,,1] - mean_Original


diff_RelabRefl_meanRelabRefl_s1 <- A_long[,,6] - mean_RelabRefl


diff_both_s1 <- bindArr(diff_Orginal_meanOriginal_s1, diff_RelabRefl_meanRelabRefl_s1, along = 3)


FA_score2_s1 <- dist(two.d.array(diff_both_s1))


Method 1 above obtained FA by total asymmetry minus DA. Two FA scores are listed since I am not sure whether squared distance or distance should be used during calculation. Method 2 obtained FA according to formula for FA shown in the figure above. FA_score1a_s1, FA_score1b_s1, and FA_score2_s1 are different. I must be wrong somewhere but I cannot figure out. I think method 1 and 2 should give identical value if calculated in the same way. So I think I must wrong somewhere. I know MorphoJ could do the calculation automatically. But I wish to know the steps behind. Coding by myself helps. I guess I am close to the answer. I would be very much appreciated if anyone could comment on the code, or directly answer by coding. Thank you.


Best regards,

YF Wen

I am looking into the source code for bilat.symmetry in geomorph v3.2.1 to understand how FA is calculated internally in bilat.symmetry. 

 

The source code for bilat.symmetry contains the following code snippet:

 

mn.DA <- DA.mns[, , 1] - DA.mns[, , 2]

...

FA.component <- simplify2array(lapply(1:n.ind, function(j) {

    t(matrix(FA.component[j, ], k, p)) + mn.shape - mn.DA

}))

 

It can be seen that mn.DA refers to difference between 1st and 2nd configuration in DA.mns. DA.mns is the DA.component in bilat.symmetry output where the first 2 configurations are original and relabeled reflections of the 1st specimen. That means FA is calculated for all specimens by the difference between relabed reflection of each specimen and its original configuration plus mean shape of original and relabled reflections of all specimens minus difference between original and relabeled reflections of the 1st specimen.

 

Based on example data and source code, I replicated bilat.symmetry results:

 

library(geomorph)

data(scallops)

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = scallops$coorddata, ind=scallops$ind)

 

A <- gpagen(scallops$coorddata)

size <- A$Csize

A <- A$coords

n <- dim(A)[3]

k <- dim(A)[2]

p <- dim(A)[1]

ind <- scallops$ind

nind <- nlevels(ind)

land.pairs <- scallops$land.pairs

npairs <- nrow(land.pairs)

A2 <- A

A2[land.pairs[, 1], , ] <- A[land.pairs[, 2], , ]

A2[land.pairs[, 2], , ] <- A[land.pairs[, 1], , ]

A2[, 1, ] <- A2[, 1, ] * (-1)

A_long <- array(c(A, A2), c(p, k, 2 * n))

ind <- factor(rep(ind, 2))

side <- gl(2, n)

gpa.res <- gpagen(A_long)

A_long <- gpa.res$coords

 

# Table specifying ordering of specimens

# row   A_long                                                scallop.sym$DA.component

# 1                   ind1                                                     ind1

# 2                   ind2                                                     ind1RelabledReflection

# 3                   ind3                                                     ind2

# 4                   ind4                                                     ind2RelabledReflection

# 5                   ind5                                                     ind3

# 6                   ind1RelabledReflection            ind3RelabledReflection

# 7                   ind2RelabledReflection          ind4

# 8                   ind3RelabledReflection            ind4RelabledReflection

# 9                   ind4RelabledReflection          ind5

# 10             ind5RelabledReflection            ind6RelabledReflection

 

scallop.sym <- bilat.symmetry(A = shape, ind = ind, object.sym = TRUE,

land.pairs=scallops$land.pairs, data = gdf, RRPP = TRUE, iter = 499)

fa_a1 <- A_long[,,6] - A_long[,,1] + mshape(A_long) - 

                        (scallop.sym$DA.component[,,1] - scallop.sym$DA.component[,,2])

                        (scallop.sym$DA.component[,,1] - scallop.sym$DA.component[,,2]) # Not (scallop.sym$DA.component[,,8] - scallop.sym$DA.component[,,7])

I do not understand why the difference between original and relabled reflection of the first specimen is subtracted when calculating FA for each specimen. I can understand adding mn.shape to t(matrix(FA.component[j, ], k, p)) allows for more meaningful interpretation and visualization. But why mn.DA is subtracted where mn.DA concerns itself with only the first specimen? The first specimen is so arbitrary.
